provider id; the session's end user must hold it.

An opaque credential handle issued for this session, resolved only at
egress. This is never a credential value.

placement.description:
How the value is sent: `bearer` (default), `header:<Name>` or
`query:<name>`.

secret.description: A Kernel Secret of this environment, by name.

label.description: The label its tools are prefixed with, unique within the agent.

memory_stores.description:
The memory stores the agent recalls from and writes to, as MemoryStore
names; at most 8.

models.description: Exact owner and cheap-tool model ids. Neither is silently substituted.

light.description:
The exact catalog id of the cheap model used only for owner-briefed
`subcall.*` tools and in-loop compaction; never an owner.

primary.description:
The exact Sylphx AI catalog id (`ai_models`) of the owner model, pinned
for the life of a session; the runtime never remaps it.

read_only.description:
Read-only: the version holds no write grant, so it may verify another
agent's work but never own it. Create and update refuse memory stores,
MCP servers, `app_function` and `client` tools, the `memory`, `browser`
and `computer` built-ins, and an HTTP tool whose pinned operation is not
GET or HEAD unless it is `runtime_only`. The `shell` and `files`
built-ins, and a `claude_code` or `codex` harness (which bring their own),
need `environment.egress` that denies by default: `DENY`, or `ALLOWLIST`
of the configured Sylphx API and inference gateways and the
version's GET or HEAD tool hosts, with no CIDRs. Session create, `:send`
and `:run` check the version and the session's effective environment
again, and refuse any model-facing credential that is not a captured
Access key holding only `<service>:read` and `ai:inference` scopes; a
renewal's `credential_updates` value for a model-facing binding is held to
the same rule. A run's `completion.result_fields` never map into the
completion tool's path or query parameters. An OwnerPool never qualifies
the version.

ttl.description:
The lease's maximum wall time, passed to Sandboxes as `ttl`. The lease

environment_mask.description:
Fields of environment to overlay, relative to EnvironmentSpec, using proto
snake_case paths such as ttl, repo.uri, repo.revision,
egress.allowed_domains and budget.max_cost_micros. The wire value is a
comma-separated string; SDK property naming does not change these paths.
Omitted or empty infers populated serialized leaf fields recursively,
preserving unselected siblings from the pinned version. Proto defaults
(including empty lists) need an explicit mask to reset a selected field.
Selected lists replace, rather than append to, the inherited list.
The sole path "*" replaces the whole environment, resetting unpopulated
fields. Unknown, invalid and output-only paths are rejected, as is a
nonempty mask without environment. Effective validation also applies to
explicit resets and whole-environment replacement.

tools.name: data_databases_create
tools.description: Creates a database. The Operation is done when the controller settles it.

database.description: The database to create; only spec and caller-writable metadata are read.

client_allowlist.description:
Address ranges allowed to connect to the database's endpoint. An entry is
an IPv4 or IPv6 range like `203.0.113.0/24` or `2001:db8::/32`, at most 50,
applied on both the pooled and the direct host a connection can reach. A
connection from any other address is refused at the endpoint with the
database's own answer (SQLSTATE 28000), before it reaches Postgres; a
connection from a listed address is served as usual. Empty serves every
address (the field absent), so clearing it re-opens the endpoint. Send
`client_allowlist_set` to store an empty list.

client_allowlist_set.description:
Stores `client_allowlist` as given, including an empty list that re-opens
the endpoint. An empty repeated field is not a change on its own, so
Update sends `client_allowlist_set` (or `clientAllowlistSet`) as `true`
when it means to clear the list; any non-empty `client_allowlist` is
stored whether or not this is set. Reads always report `false`.

compute_units.description:
Compute size in units; default the plan's. `max_connections` derives from
it.

deletion_protection.description: While set, Delete fails with DELETION_PROTECTED.

postgres_version.description:
The Postgres major version, for example `17`; default the newest
supported.

region.description:
The region; default the project's home region. Changing it moves the data
by signed export and import.

database_id.description: The id segment of the name; the server assigns one when unset.

validate_only.description: Validate and return the result without writing anything.

annotations.title: Creates a database. The Operation is done when the controller settles it.

tools.name: knowledge_remember
tools.description:
Records an episode and returns at once (`remember`); extraction reads
it afterwards.

episode.description: The episode to create; only caller-writable fields are read.

data.description:
Structured content, for a caller that already knows the shape (an
imported row, a form).

entities.description:
The entities the caller says the episode is about, as resource names;
extraction adds the ones it finds. At most 50.

occur_time.description: When it happened in the world; default the time it was recorded.

provenance.description: Where it came from and who wrote it.

method.description:
How the content was produced; default `SOURCE_METHOD_STATED`. Only the
service writes `SOURCE_METHOD_EXTRACTED`.

references.description:
References to where the content came from: a run and step, a work item,
a message, a URL. At most 20.

items.description: A SourceRef points at where a record's content came from.

label.description: A short label to show with a citation.

pinned_version.description: Immutable version of the source observed when this claim was recorded.

uri.description: A URI: a URL, or a URN of a platform record such as a Workflows run step.

text.description:
The text as written, at most 64 KiB. An episode has `text`, `data`, or
both.

episode_id.description:
The episode id, the final name segment; the server assigns one when
empty.

skip_extraction.description:
Record the episode without extraction, for content that is already
structured or must not be read by a model.

validate_only.description: Validate and return the result without writing anything.

annotations.title: Records an episode and returns at once (`remember`); extraction reads it afterwards.

tools.name: knowledge_recall
tools.description:
Searches the graph (`recall`): hybrid lexical and semantic search over
episodes and facts, fused by reciprocal rank, then at most two hops of
expansion from the top entities. Returns a context pack with citations,
built only from records the caller may see.

entity_types.description: Only entities of these types; default every type.

max_facts.description: At most this many facts in the pack; default 30, clamped to 200.

max_hops.description: How many hops to expand from the top entities, 0 to 2; default 2.

parent.description: The environment whose graph to search.

query.description: What to recall, in natural language; 1 to 4000 characters.

spaces.description:
The spaces to search, as resource names; default every space the caller
may read. At most 50.

valid_time.description: Recall the graph as it was valid at this time; default now.

annotations.title: Searches the graph (`recall`): hybrid lexical and semantic search over episodes and facts, fused by reciprocal rank, then at most two hops of expansion from the top entities. Returns a context pack with citations, built only from records the caller may see.

tools.description:

filter.description: AIP-160 filter over the typed, allowlisted fields.

page_size.description: At most this many; default 100, clamped to 1000.

page_token.description:
`next_page_token` of the previous page; bound to tenant, interval, filter,
and order.

parent.description: The parent the method acts in.

start_time.description: The interval start; required, at most 31 days before `end_time`.

annotations.title: Queries the environment's log entries over a bounded interval; follow a trace with `trace_id = "..."`.

page_token.description:

and order.

parent.description: The parent the method acts in.

start_time.description: The interval start; required, at most 31 days before `end_time`.

tools.name: observability_generations_get
tools.description: Gets a generation: one Sylphx AI call.

name.description: The name of the generation to get.

annotations.title: Gets a generation: one Sylphx AI call.

tools.description:
Lists the environment's Sylphx AI calls, newest first, within the trace

tools.name: workflows_schedule
tools.description:
Updates a schedule; with `allow_missing` it creates the schedule when it
does not exist, so its short name `schedule` is an upsert by name.

allow_missing.description: Create the schedule when it does not exist (declarative upsert).

schedule.description: The schedule to update; `name` identifies it.

calendar.description: A calendar: cron expression and time zone.

catchup_window.description: Missed fires older than this are skipped; 10s to 365d.

input.description: The input of every Run, at most 64 KiB of JSON.

jitter.description: Random delay added to each fire, at most min(interval, 1h).

overlap_policy.description: What a fire does while a previous Run is still running.

pause_note.description: Why the Schedule is paused; shown in status.

workflow.description: The Workflow the Schedule starts, in the same environment.

update_mask.description: The fields to write; unset writes every populated field.

validate_only.description: Validate and return the result without writing anything.

annotations.title: Updates a schedule; with `allow_missing` it creates the schedule when it does not exist, so its short name `schedule` is an upsert by name.

tools.name: workflows_start
tools.description:
Starts a Run of a Workflow, now or after `start_delay` or at
`schedule_time`. `run_id` is the caller's key: the same key and intent
return the same Run, a changed intent is refused.
An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is
`USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.

run.description: The run to create; only caller-writable fields are read.

input.description: The Run input, at most 256 KiB of JSON.

schedule_time.description:
When the first invocation is due: set it directly, or through
`start_delay`; at most 365 days ahead. A Run cancelled before then closes
`cancelled` with no invocation.

start_delay.description: Delay the first invocation by this much.

run_id.description: The run id, the final name segment; the server assigns one when empty.

validate_only.description: Validate and return the result without writing anything.

annotations.title: Starts a Run of a Workflow, now or after `start_delay` or at `schedule_time`. `run_id` is the caller's key: the same key and intent return the same Run, a changed intent is refused. An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is `USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.

tools.name: workflows_signal
tools.description:
Sends a named signal to a running Run; a `wait` op for that name resumes
with its payload. A signal to a closed Run fails with INVALID_STATE.
An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is
`USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.

payload.description: The signal payload, at most 64 KiB of JSON.

signal.description: The signal name the handler waits on.

annotations.title: Sends a named signal to a running Run; a `wait` op for that name resumes with its payload. A signal to a closed Run fails with INVALID_STATE. An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is `USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.

tools.name: workflows_cancel
tools.description:
Requests cancellation. Timers and waits stop; a running invocation is not
interrupted: the handler receives one final invocation with `cancel:
true`, and the Run ends `cancelled` when it answers.
An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is
`USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.

confirm.description: Must be true: this call destroys or revokes.

annotations.title: Requests cancellation. Timers and waits stop; a running invocation is not interrupted: the handler receives one final invocation with `cancel: true`, and the Run ends `cancelled` when it answers. An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is `USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.

tools.name: workflows_result
tools.description:
Waits up to `timeout` (at most 60s) for the Run to close, then returns it,
closed or not. Its short name is `result`: the closed Run carries the
handler's output or error.
An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is
`USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.

timeout.description: How long to wait; default 30s, at most 60s.

annotations.title: Waits up to `timeout` (at most 60s) for the Run to close, then returns it, closed or not. Its short name is `result`: the closed Run carries the handler's output or error. An end user's session may call it on a Workflow whose `callers` is `USERS` when the session holds the Workflow's `permission`.

tools.description: Load one skill from an immutable AgentVersion. Use the version pinned by your session, not the agent's current version.

instructions: Sylphx is one API for every Sylphx service. Call access_whoami first to learn your org, project, and env. Resource names are full paths such as orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/databases/{id}. Use sylphx_search_methods to find a method, sylphx_describe_method for its input schema, and sylphx_call to call it; destructive methods need confirm: true.
